target_customer: School districts and state education agencies that buy K-12 hiring software
problem: Districts struggle to identify strong teacher applicants and track vacancies. Nimble offers an applicant tracking system with predictive analytics to highlight likely high performers.
business_model: B2B SaaS contracts with districts and states, plus federal research grants
product_category: K-12 applicant tracking and hiring analytics

founders.name: Lauren Dachille
prior_employers: D.C. Public Schools (Recruitment and Selection team)
education: MBA, Stanford Graduate School of Business
B.S. Human Development and Education, Cornell University

investors: Institute of Education Sciences (SBIR Phase II)

competitors.name: TeacherMatch
competitors.what: Chicago-based predictive teacher candidate assessment sold to districts
competitors.traction_then: Working with hundreds of districts per 2013 and 2014 coverage
competitors.funding_then: Sold to PeopleAdmin in May 2016 (amount undisclosed)

technical_complexity.rationale: An applicant tracking system with a predictive model is standard SaaS plus modest machine learning, though validating teacher quality predictions needs district data.

defensibility.rationale: Established vendors held district relationships, so copying the predictive layer was feasible, but district contracts and state partnerships create some stickiness.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: TeacherMatch was later shut down per North Carolina's education department, and Nimble survived. No acquisition of Nimble found.

market_need_then: Teacher hiring was a recognized pain: 2013 EdWeek coverage described districts adopting predictive tools, though experts said evidence of accuracy was thin. The founder says she lost time to hiring spreadsheets at D.C. Public Schools.

identity.voice_and_tone: Clarity, speed and confidence for K-12 hiring

branding.community_and_virality: Features in Forbes, Education Week and EdSurge per the company site. No merch or fan evidence found.

brand_strength.rationale: Name is generic and shared with other companies called Nimble, and sources show little brand-specific press.

pivots.from: District applicant tracking with predictive scoring
pivots.to: State partnerships with vacancy reporting, licensure pathways and matching
pivots.why: Company site lists Insight, Discover, Navigate, Connect and Hire products and states it partners with states. The date and reason were not stated.

outcome_analysis: Nimble joined YC in Summer 2017 with a predictive teacher hiring tool and survives as a public benefit corporation. No venture rounds beyond the YC deal were found, while federal SBIR awards of $200,000 in 2021 and $1,000,000 in 2024 fund research and product work. It moved toward state education agency partnerships. It has not shown venture-scale traction in the sources found, so the outcome is stable but modest.
notes: Aggregators conflict on total raised ($120K on CB Insights, $1M on Wellfound) and are not recorded as rounds. A federal SBIR profile lists Jill Greenberg as co-founder, but only one source does, so she is not recorded as a founder. Founding year is 2016 per EdWeek and 2017 per YC. TeacherMatch source for competition is a 2013 article, and the May 2016 sale date is from a search result about Arma Partners. The AppliTrack link is a current Frontline page without a date, listed from the search that identified Frontline as former AppliTrack. Grants are recorded as stage grant, not equity rounds.
